pr_body:

issue_context.title: Improve bluetooth tester application
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
Bluetooth tester application grew a lot since its introduction and we need some cleanups (and possibly refactor) to handle more services (ie le audio related)

**Describe the solution you'd like**
BTP handling code needs to be refactored and cleanup to allow maintainable grow of supported services.

review_comments: I appreciate that this is how it was done before, and how `hci.h` also does it, but we could also consider putting the commands into an `enum` as recommended by https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/v4.10/process/coding-style.html#macros-enums-and-rtl
I have mixed feelings about using enums for protocols parsing as comparing value outside of enum specified range is not defined

> as comparing value outside of enum specified range is not defined

I'm not sure I follow that; can you elaborate?

Ah, yes, I see what you mean. 

On the other hand, if we have a switch for `cp->chr` after the cast, the enum type should help us ensure that all cases of the enum has been handled in that switch. 

So using an `enum` "forces" us to handle out-of-range values. 

e.g.

```c
switch (cp->chr) {
case BTP_PACS_CHARACTERISTIC_SINK_PAC:
    break;
default:
    break;
}
```
should give a warning, since `BTP_PACS_CHARACTERISTIC_SOURCE_PAC` hasn't been handled.

I am, however, not sure if a warning would appear if the `default` case isn't there.
but this is the case exactly I'm not liking about using enums for this,    doing switch on enum while value is outside of valid range

Would it make sense to statically register the handlers? 
Would it be possible to simply have a static array of handlers like 
```c
static const struct event_handler normal_events
``` 
from `hci_core.c`?
this is how BTP works,  ie services are registered (enabled) on demand
